releases.name: Pydantic AI capability 0.1.0
releases.body:
Independent FlashData capability for Pydantic AI 2.61.

- 14 selectable Google/YouTube query tools, with deferred approval and pricing/job/result reads through the existing MCP endpoint.
- A separate protected local CLI workflow for media delivery, completing the 15-task guide.
- Serializable agent specs, per-run MCP sessions, no automatic paid-call retries, and documented service/cost boundaries.

Install the Python package from this fixed Git tag using the package README. Users provide their own FlashData key and paid Credits; model/storage fees are separate.

Validation uses the real Pydantic AI host with synthetic MCP responses and disabled external sockets: 30 tests, wheel/sdist checks, clean wheel installation, and Python 3.11/3.14 CI. No live paid retrieval, model request, or storage write is claimed. PyPI publication and official ecosystem listing are separate and are not established by this source release.

releases.name: FlashData Skills for OpenCode and Pi v0.1.0
releases.body:
Install 15 FlashData task Skills in OpenCode or Pi from this Git release. OpenCode uses the small local plugin; Pi uses the repository's declared Skills. See [installation and capability guides](https://github.com/rocosen/flashdata-mcp/tree/agent-skills-v0.1.0/packages/agent-skills).

Software installation is free. Data queries use the user's own FlashData API key and paid Credits. The package does not execute queries on installation.

Validated with OpenCode 1.19.4 and Pi 1.4.0 through isolated installation and discovery of all 15 Skills. Adapter contract, generated-content and packaging checks passed; Linux, Windows and Docker CI passed. OpenCode v2 was checked against its interface, without a live v2 host run. No model call, paid data query or customer-storage write was performed.

This is one Git distribution covering 15 capabilities. npm publication and official OpenCode/Pi directory listings are separate and are not claimed by this release.

releases.name: FlashData for Haystack v0.1.0
releases.body:
FlashData components for Haystack 3.4 Pipelines and Agents: 15 Google/YouTube capabilities, 17 components, and 15 task-specific examples.

Install from this source tag:

```bash
pip install "git+https://github.com/rocosen/flashdata-mcp.git@haystack-v0.1.0#subdirectory=packages/haystack"
```

Use `FLASHDATA_API_KEY` via Haystack Secret. Installation is MIT/free; API requests consume paid FlashData Credits. YouTube delivery requires customer storage and explicit `allow_submit=True` configuration; status/result reads do not create new jobs. No automatic retry or polling.

Validated with 79 network-disabled tests, Python 3.11/3.14 CI, wheel/sdist checks and a clean installation. These checks do not represent production API/model/storage execution. PyPI publication and Haystack directory review are separate; neither is implied by this source release.

releases.name: FlashData Python task CLIs v0.1.0 — 15 capabilities
releases.body:
Fifteen independent Python JSON CLIs, one per FlashData capability. Each includes its input schema, task guide and MIT license. These are the already-tested 0.1.0 distributions built from commit 0849f7c6d797f102bef56da0f787c8b345386278; SHA256SUMS lists all 30 artifacts.

Install a downloaded wheel in an isolated Python 3.10+ environment, or use the FlashData Homebrew tap once its formulae are merged. The 15 project names are listed in packages/python-cli/packages.json at this tag. Help, version and schema commands run without a key or API request.

PyPI publication is still pending: the uvx/PyPI commands in the bundled package READMEs require that later publication. This GitHub release does not publish to PyPI and does not change existing npm packages.

Installation is free. Actual queries require your FlashData API Key and paid Credits; delivery to customer cloud storage additionally requires explicit submission authorization and storage configuration. No model is invoked, and no paid request runs during installation. See https://flashdata.dev/pricing and the per-source documentation linked from each package.

Validation: 64 offline tests, Python 3.10/3.14 CI, wheel/sdist metadata checks and all 15 isolated/shared-environment installation checks. All artifact hashes and runtime source files were rechecked before upload.

releases.name: Smithery task servers v0.1.1 — 15 independent entries
releases.body:
Repository migration (2026-10-15): copied from `flashdata-dev/flashdata-mcp` at tag `smithery-task-servers-v0.1.1`. Original Git history and asset bytes are preserved. This copy does not replace existing package provenance or indicate new platform approval.

---

15 independent local MCP servers for Google Search, News, Images, Shopping, Video Search and Places; YouTube Search, Extended Search, Metadata, Transcript, Captions, Trainability, Channel Data, Autocomplete and Download.

Choose one MCPB bundle for the task you need. Each bundle runs locally with Node.js 22.18+ and includes its production dependencies. It exposes one fixed data source plus source-restricted pricing, job and result reads. Use your own FlashData API Key. Installation is free; FlashData API calls are paid. Smithery/client/model plans are separate.

[Smithery listings and usage guides](https://github.com/flashdata-dev/flashdata-mcp/blob/main/smithery/README.md)

Version 0.1.1 corrects realtime response examples to `status: done`, documents the observed Add to toolbox / sign-in flow, and keeps supporting-tool descriptions within each task. Async job status remains `completed`.

Validation: all 15 final 0.1.1 bundles passed isolated stdio contracts, public-content checks and authenticated Smithery download SHA-256 verification. Real free tools/list and pricing checks passed for all 15 initial 0.1.0 bundles; 0.1.1 changes documentation/descriptions only and did not repeat live calls. Linux and Windows CI passed. No paid data query, model call or real storage write was performed. Successful publication does not imply search indexing or customer acquisition.

`index.json` includes the SHA-256 digest, size, fixed source and tools for each bundle. The original combined npm package and hosted Smithery entry remain available.
